s1.syndrome_frame: Post-liver transplantation fulminant liver failure with hemodynamic shock and cholestasis
salient_findings: Intra-abdominal bleeding from a choledochal artery branch
key_facts: 52-year-old man with HCV-associated end-stage cirrhosis
Underwent liver transplantation
Required relaparotomy due to intra-abdominal bleeding
Initial liver function improved
Cholestasis observed on day 4
Persistent abdominal pain reported on day 6
Fulminant liver failure and hemodynamic shock developed by day 7
Single fever peak of 38.4°C on day 8
Elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT, GGT, ALP) on day 6
Total bilirubin level of 119 μmol/L on day 6
Positive blood culture on day 7
Positive liver graft, colon, and small bowel biopsy samples on day 9

shortlist.label: Primary Graft Dysfunction
shortlist.why_kept: Initial liver function improvement followed by fulminant liver failure

shortlist.label: Graft Rejection
shortlist.why_kept: Cholestasis and worsening cytolysis after initial improvement

shortlist.label: Sepsis-induced Cholestasis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive blood culture and hemodynamic shock

shortlist.label: Hepatitis C Virus Recurrence
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of HCV-associated end-stage cirrhosis

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus Hepatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fever peak and liver dysfunction in an immunocompromised patient

raw.rationale: The patient developed fulminant liver failure, hemodynamic shock, and had positive blood cultures, indicating a severe infection. The timeline of events, including the onset of cholestasis and worsening cytolysis after an initial improvement in liver function, along with the presence of sepsis markers (fever, positive blood culture), supports sepsis-induced cholestasis as the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Primary Graft Dysfunction
rejected.why: While possible, the improvement in initial liver function followed by deterioration suggests a secondary event rather than primary dysfunction.

rejected.label: Graft Rejection
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence of graft rejection, such as histopathological findings or a clear temporal relationship with immunosuppression changes.

rejected.label: Hepatitis C Virus Recurrence
rejected.why: The rapid progression to fulminant liver failure and the presence of sepsis markers make recurrence less likely as the primary cause at this stage.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus Hepatitis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided for CMV infection, such as positive CMV PCR or histological findings, to support this diagnosis over sepsis-induced cholestasis.

gold: Listeria monocytogenes infection in a liver transplant recipient
